traceability.notes:
Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION is fully implemented.
The ESLint rule `require-test-traceability` exists, is wired into the plugin, and is covered by focused tests. It enforces: - File-level `@supports` annotations in test files (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS) using `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation`, with clear error messaging and optional placeholder auto-fix. - Story references in `describe`/top-level test blocks via a configurable regex pattern (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE). - `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes in `it`/`test` names, including detection and normalization of malformed prefixes (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT). - Selective application to test files based on configurable `testFilePatterns` (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT). - Compatibility with Jest and Mocha-style APIs by recognizing `describe`, `it`, `test`, and `context`, and handling member forms like `describe.each` (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT).
Existing rules from dependency stories (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) provide the deeper validation for story paths and requirement IDs referenced in `@supports`, satisfying REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID when the plugin is used as documented. User-facing documentation in `user-docs/api-reference.md` and README describes the rule’s behavior, options, and usage in detail. The dedicated Jest test file for this rule passes as part of the full test suite, confirming behavior matches the specification. Therefore this story is assessed as PASSED.
